text:
Tom Nguyen: Hi team — after switching our embedding calls to use the int8 quantization profile, we started getting embeddings of length 768, but our app expects 1536. Example error: "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768". This started ~10:30am UTC and affects production. Anyone seen this?

Priya Patel: thanks for reporting — can you paste the exact request payload + model name you're calling? also any headers like x-redwood-model or model pinning?

Tom Nguyen: sure, here's the curl we use (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1536","input":["doc1","doc2"],"precision":"int8","batch_size":16}'
```

Tom Nguyen: response snippet: `{"data":[{"embedding":[...] , "dim":768}, ...]}`

Marta Ruiz: quick thought — quantization (fp16/int8) shouldn't change vector dimensionality. If you're getting 768 instead of 1536, that usually means the service routed to a different model family (e.g., redwood-embed-768) or a compressed variant. Are you using any routing policies or model aliasing?

Tom Nguyen: We didn't set any alias. We do have a Dedicated deployment with a fallback policy to reduce cost during spikes. Could that cause a different variant to be used?

Jared Cole: yes — smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained. The important bit: compatible in terms of API (embedding endpoint) but not necessarily identical dims. There should be logs showing fallback decisions.

Tom Nguyen: ugh. How can we confirm? We don't see an explicit header in the response that tells the model id used.

Priya Patel: we can check request trace in Console and inspect the per-request metadata (model_used). Could you share the request ids from one or two failing calls? or toggle verbose header `X-Debug-Trace: 1` in staging to capture trace.

Tom Nguyen: here's one request id: req_63a9b8f2. I'll paste the raw response we stored for that req below.

```json
{"id":"req_63a9b8f2","model_requested":"redwood-embed-1536","model_used":"redwood-embed-768-int8","embedding_dim":768,"notes":"fallback due to dedicated pool saturated"}
```

Tom Nguyen: so yep looks like fallback to `redwood-embed-768-int8`. That caused the mismatch.

Marta Ruiz: yep — this explains it. Two main root causes we see in these escalations: 1) routing fallback to a variant with different dimensionality, 2) client-side assumptions (hard-coded dim). Fixes: pin model version strictly (e.g., `model: "redwood-embed-1536@v2"`) or change fallback policy, or update client to handle multiple dims if acceptable.

Jared Cole: for throughput/batching concerns — note that batching itself won't change dims, but if you have dynamic batching + fallback, latency spikes can trigger fallback policies. Also some Dedicated configs allow "cost-optimized fallback" which trades to a smaller model.

Tom Nguyen: is there a way to get a non-fallback guarantee for a period (we need consistent dims for a release)?

Priya Patel: yes — two options: 1) temporarily pin to the exact model variant (we can help create a deployment reservation for redwood-embed-1536) or 2) set `allow_fallback=false` in your Dedicated policy so the control plane returns an explicit capacity error instead of silently falling back. Which do you prefer?

Tom Nguyen: prefer option 2 for now — fail loudly so our pipeline can degrade gracefully. How do we set that?

Marta Ruiz: you can update the Dedicated config in Console: Routing -> Fallback policy -> toggle `Allow model variant fallback` = off. Or via API: 

```http
PATCH /v1/dedicated/{pool_id}/routing
{ "allow_fallback": false }
```

Marta Ruiz: after you flip that, any request when the pool is saturated will return 429 with a `x-redwood-error: capacity_exceeded` header rather than returning a different-dim embedding.

Tom Nguyen: sweet. We'll flip it and run smoke tests. One more Q: the initial confusion was also about `precision` — will switching between fp16 and int8 ever change dims?

Marta Ruiz: no. Precision changes the numeric representation (dtype) and sometimes how vectors are stored/transmitted, but the semantic embedding size (number of floats) is model architecture dependent, not precision dependent. fp16 vs int8 affects memory/cost/latency and can slightly change embedding values (quantization noise) but not the length.

Tom Nguyen: ok good to know — we were worried int8 might halve dims.

Jared Cole: for perf: int8 will usually improve throughput and lower memory but watch quality drift. For critical similarity tasks, run an eval on a held-out prompt set and compare cosine similarity distribution between fp16 and int8. If quality drop > your threshold, use fp16 or consider a mixed-precision profile.

Priya Patel: action items for us/support: 1) we flagged the customer's pool fallback logs and suggested toggle; 2) sent a note to infra to check why pool saturated at that window (spike or autoscale misconfig). 3) provide guidance doc snippet for customers about model pinning vs fallback and embedding dims.

embed-bot: [notice] autoscaler event at 1769801305 — scaled down pool from 6->4 GPUs due to policy `min_idle_time` hit.

Jared Cole: that autoscaler event likely coincides with the fallback window. We'll look into if the `min_idle_time` is too aggressive.

Tom Nguyen: flipped `allow_fallback=false` and retried — got 429 as expected. We'll schedule a maintenance window to reserve capacity for next release. Thanks all.

Priya Patel: glad that worked. We'll stay on the thread while you validate. If you want, we can also patch your client to validate embedding length in the SDK and raise a clearer error to avoid silent downstream issues.

Tom Nguyen: yes please — a pre-flight check in SDK would have saved us :), thanks.

Marta Ruiz: will draft a short SDK PR that asserts returned dimension matches the model metadata. Also adding a note in docs: "quantization does not change dims; routing may."

Tom Nguyen: confirming everything green after a 5-min smoke: no more dim mismatches. Appreciate the quick triage. :party_popper:

Priya Patel: closing for now; reopen if you see more incidents. Thanks team!
